title: Quake's inverse square root used a magic hexadecimal number
body: Games need 1/sqrt(x) constantly for lighting. Quake III's 1999 code reinterpreted a float's bits as an integer, subtracted them from 0x5f3759df, and got an astonishingly good first guess, refined by one Newton step. Why that constant works requires viewing floats as approximate logarithms, which is exactly the trick.
